### Observed differences

- Routing out of A02 shifted toward the A03 route: before, about 43 in 100 of A02's outgoing transitions went to A03 and about 31 in 100 to A04 (with about 20 to A07 and 6 back to A01); in the later window, about 50 in 100 went to A03 and only about 21 to A04, while the A07 and A01 shares stayed similar. [DIR002]
- The A03–A17 route therefore ran more often: A03 and A17 each appeared in about 47 in 100 traces before versus about 54 in 100 in the later window, occurring about 1.5 versus about 2.3 times per trace; A03 was followed by A17 in essentially every instance in both windows. [OCC002, OCC016, DIR003]
- The A04 branch ran less often: A04 appeared in about 61 in 100 traces before versus about 48 later (mean about 1.3 versus 1.1 occurrences per trace), A14 fell from about 61 to 48 in 100, and A13's mean fell from about 0.71 to 0.60 (a weak signal); within the branch, the A04 split between A13 and A14 stayed roughly 54/46 in both windows. [OCC003, OCC012, OCC013, DIR004]
- Activities on and below the A03/A17 route were executed more often: A05 rose from about 29 to 41 in 100 traces (mean about 0.67 to 1.17), A07 from about 40 to 53, A15 from about 22 to 38, A11 from about 18 to 27 and A12 from about 40 to 53; A06 and A10 rose slightly. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC014]
- A second routing shift occurred at A07: the share of A07's outgoing transitions continuing to A15 rose from about 20% to 30%, while the share to A09 fell from about 30% to 20% (A08 steady near 50%); A07 and A15 co-occurred in about 22% versus 38% of traces, and A15 never came first in either window — the pair either ran A07 then A15 or was interleaved/repeated, both patterns more frequent in the later window. [DIR005, REL001]
- Repetitions per trace also rose: A02, present in every trace in both windows, averaged about 1.9 occurrences per trace before versus about 2.2 later and repeated in about 47% versus 54% of traces; A15 self-repetitions (seen only at distances of 2 and 4 steps) rose from 11 to 25 observed pairs with the same gap pattern. [OCC001, LAG002]
- Placement did not change: the positions of A07 and A15 within traces and the distances between A07 and A15 stayed essentially the same; only their frequencies moved. [POS001, POS002, LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that existing alternative paths were taken with different frequencies. In the later window, at A02 the route via A03 — which leads to A17 in virtually every case — was taken more often (about 50% of A02's outgoing transitions versus about 43% before) while the route to A04 was taken less often (about 21% versus 31%); at A07, the route to A15 was taken more often (about 30% versus 20%) and the route to A09 less often (about 20% versus 30%). Accordingly, A03, A17, A05, A07, A15, A11 and A12 appeared in more traces and occurred more often per trace, while A04, A13 and A14 appeared in fewer traces. [DIR002, DIR005, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC006, OCC010, OCC011, OCC013, OCC014, OCC016, REL001]

The routing shifts are shown directly by the transition shares out of A02 and A07 and match the occurrence changes in direction and rough size; the internal split of the A04 branch (A13 versus A14) did not move, so that branch lost traffic overall rather than being rerouted internally; and the unchanged positions and step distances argue against a relocation or reordering of activities as the explanation. [DIR002, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, LAG001]

The main competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is sampling variability between the two 200-trace windows: no screening baseline is provided to compare the number of qualifying items against what an unchanged process would produce, several items describe the same traces (the A03 and A17 occurrence profiles are identical, and the A07–A15 relation appears in both a transition and a relation item, so agreements are not independent), and the weakest items (A13, A08, A09, A16) would not distinguish a change from chance on their own. [OCC002, OCC007, OCC008, OCC012, OCC015, OCC016, DIR005, REL001]

Other differences: Repetitions per trace increased beyond what the rerouting alone explains — A02 recurred in about 47% versus 54% of traces (mean about 1.9 versus 2.2 occurrences) and A15 self-repeated more often (11 versus 25 pairs, unchanged gap pattern) — and two smaller share shifts appeared, from A17 toward A05 (about 43% to 50%) and from A15 toward A11 (about 46% to 53%). [OCC001, LAG002, DIR009, DIR008]
